standard.title: Halves, quarters and eighths in context
standard.description: identify common uses and represent halves, quarters and eighths in relation to shapes, objects and events
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have informally explored equal sharing (AC9M1N06). They have not yet identified halves, quarters and eighths in measurement and time contexts or connected the fraction language to real-world uses.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify common uses of halves, quarters and eighths and represent them in relation to shapes, objects and events including length, position, time and everyday measurement contexts.

nodes.label: Halves and quarters in shapes and objects
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and represent halves and quarters of shapes and objects, confirming that parts are equal.
nodes.minimum_width: Fold or cut a shape into halves; then into quarters by halving again; confirm all parts are equal.
nodes.typical_width: Represent halves and quarters of shapes, paper and food objects by folding or cutting; explain that parts must be equal; connect language (half, quarter) to the fraction symbol and to repeated halving.
wider: Demonstrate how food items (sandwiches, pizzas, cakes) can be cut into halves, quarters and eighths by halving twice; ensure parts are equal
Investigate cup and spoon measures in cooking: what half or quarter of a cup means; compare half-cup to full cup using sand or water
success_criteria: Folds or cuts a shape into halves with equal parts
Creates quarters from a half by halving again and confirms all four parts are equal

nodes.label: Halves and quarters in length and position
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and use halves and quarters to describe positions and distances in familiar contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and mark the halfway point on a given length or path.
nodes.typical_width: Use halves and quarters to describe lengths, positions and distances; e.g. mark the halfway point in a race, the quarter-way mark, and stand halfway between two objects.
wider: Use halves and quarters to describe positions on a number line, ruler length, or path between two points; relate to fractions of a whole length
Investigate positions on a classroom map or grid using halves and quarters
success_criteria: Identifies the halfway point on a given length or distance
Uses the word 'quarter' to describe a position one-quarter of the way along a length

nodes.label: Halves and quarters in time and events
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify halves and quarters of an hour and connect fraction language to real-world time and event contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify half an hour and quarter of an hour; connect to clock positions (half past, quarter past).
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and use halves and quarters in time contexts: half an hour, quarter of an hour, half time and quarters in sporting events; connect to clock language and to the clock face as a circle divided into halves and quarters.
wider: Discuss how sirens in Australian Rules Football represent quarters and half-time; connect to the clock face as a circle divided by quarter-turns
Investigate other events or activities that use halves and quarters of time (e.g. cooking timers, race laps); explain what each fraction refers to

response_modes.reason: This node brings together the abstract fraction concept (equal parts of a whole) and time as a measurement context. The integration challenge is connecting 'quarter of an hour' to both the numerical fraction (15 out of 60 minutes) and the physical clock face (one quarter of the circle).

success_criteria: Identifies half an hour and a quarter of an hour in a given context
Connects 'half past' and 'quarter past' to the position of the big hand on a clock face
